title: Fintech: UPI-style Payments (PayZippy and friends)
description: A fictional UPI-style digital payments ecosystem with five payment apps, eight banks and 400 merchants across India. Transactions cover P2P transfers, merchant payments, bill payments and recharges over two years, with salary-day, festive and evening peaks plus four NammaPay outages. Use it for failure-rate analysis, peak-hour load, merchant category insights and simple fraud-flag exploration.

qualityIssues: transactions: ~0.4% (about 90) rows are exact duplicates (same txn_id), so txn_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint; users: 10 exact duplicate rows; failed_transactions: 6 exact duplicates.
transactions.merchant_id is NULL for P2P rows (~24%) and receiver_user_id is NULL for non-P2P rows - by design, not an error.
users.city ~10% inconsistent casing/whitespace and ~3% NULL; users.phone ~2% NULL; users.upi_id ~5% NULL; merchants.city ~8% inconsistent casing.
failed_transactions.retry_succeeded is NULL when retried = 0 (~40% of rows).
CSV only - users.signup_date: ~15% of rows are DD-MM-YYYY.
CSV only - transactions.txn_datetime: ~15% DD-MM-YYYY HH:MM:SS; transactions.amount: ~12% text with rupee symbol and Indian grouping.

signals: [Instructor note] Kaveri Co-op Bank has a much higher failure rate than other banks, concentrated in peak hours (9-10h and 18-20h) with code BANK_SERVER_TIMEOUT (about 15% at peak vs ~2% elsewhere).

[Instructor note] NammaPay had four outage windows (2023-03-14 10-13h, 2023-09-21 18-22h, 2024-02-06 9-12h, 2024-07-16 19-22h). Inside them about 42% of NammaPay attempts fail with UPI_SYSTEM_DOWN, vs ~2-3% normally.
[Instructor note] Failures are ~35% higher on the 1st-3rd of the month (salary days) and amounts above 50,000 fail 2.5x more (LIMIT_EXCEEDED).
[Instructor note] Volume spikes around Diwali windows and month-end; weekends are ~10% higher; evening 18-20h is the busiest slot.
[Instructor note] Network/timeouts are retried and succeed far more often than insufficient-funds failures.

[Instructor note] About 1.5% of transactions are flagged (is_flagged = 1). Flags cluster in late-night hours (23h-4h), in accounts less than 30 days old, when an amount is more than 3x the payer's usual median, and for Electronics, Travel and Entertainment merchants. Large late-night P2P transfers (> 8,000) are the strongest signal (~30% flagged).
[Instructor note] Customer activity is heavy-tailed; merchant volume is power-law distributed; Fuel/Travel/Electronics have high ticket sizes.
